I have 20 mu to work this year. This land is cotton country — been that way since my father's time. I will put cotton on 10 mu like last year, and the other 10 mu I do wheat in winter then maize in summer, two crops one year. That way the family has grain and the cotton brings cash.

Cotton I know best after 53 years. I buy the Bt hybrid seed from the same dealer in town — everyone uses it now, bollworm doesn't eat it so bad anymore. Before planting in April I plough deep, then spread 2 bags of 15-15-15 compound per mu, that's about 100 jin. When the plants come up strong I topdress urea twice, half a bag each time. Cotton drinks water — I pump from the well 3 times through summer. Still have to spray aphids and the bollworm that gets through, about 6 times a season. Last year I got around 250 jin of seed cotton per mu, this year I want the same.

Wheat I plant in October after the maize comes off. I broadcast improved seed from the station, about 20 jin per mu. Put 1.5 bags compound fertilizer as base before rotary tilling, then topdress half a bag urea in spring when it turns green. Three waterings — planting, jointing, before heading. Two sprays for aphids and rust. About 450 jin per mu is normal.

Maize comes after wheat in June. I no-till drill hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958, same as the neighbors — right into the wheat stubble, saves diesel and time. One bag compound at planting, one bag urea at big trumpet stage. Two waterings from the well, one spray for corn borer. Around 500 jin per mu.

Fertilizer costs are high now so I don't want to waste, but I would rather put a little extra than have weak plants. Every jin of yield lost is more money than a bag of urea.
